items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I had an opportunity during the period that I was with Trent to know these things... Alphonso was the piano player. He liked me and he used to... then I used to start bugging him to show me things.

ctx.x: Yeah, but that's kind of unusual, because at that time music teachers were, you know...

Was real strict, you know, the eighth note, hit your hand...why didn't you see that accidental, that's an eighth note, that's a B-flat, and so forth. But she said that to me. And then I paid attention to that. But Bud Goldberg, who was the manager of Alphonso Trent's orchestra, came up to a dance in the black community with Trent. And he saw me out on the floor dancing, and everybody was crowded around me, you know, when you're a crowd-seeker, you know, and he said to Trent, "Why don't we take that dancer and let…

me and then I'd get a lot of tips. So this is how I really broke into like what I call the big time. But one of the things that happened was, that sitting behind that piano for three or four hours, I had an opportunity to really listen at changes--hearing a guy play a different kind of thing, or hear now the trumpets coming in, or the piano would be playing--this is a piano solo or clarinet solo, so I had an opportunity during the period that I was with Trent to know these things, which didn't hurt.
